subChunks.title: Flexbox Layout
subChunks.hookHtml: Flexbox is one of the two layout primitives that power nearly every UI on the web. If you can build a nav bar, a card with side-by-side content, and a centred hero — you can build most of what a junior front-end role demands.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Activating flex

flex         /* display: flex        */
inline-flex  /* display: inline-flex */

Flex direction

flex-row          /* children go left to right (default) */
flex-col          /* children stack top to bottom        */
flex-row-reverse
flex-col-reverse

Align items (cross axis)

items-start     /* flex-start  */
items-center    /* center      */
items-end       /* flex-end    */
items-stretch   /* default     */
items-baseline

Justify content (main axis)

justify-start    /* flex-start         */
justify-center   /* center             */
justify-end      /* flex-end           */
justify-between  /* space-between      */
justify-around   /* space-around       */
justify-evenly   /* space-evenly       */

Flex children: grow and shrink

flex-1     /* grows AND shrinks to fill available space */
flex-auto  /* grows and shrinks based on content size  */
flex-none  /* fixed size, never grows or shrinks       */
grow       /* flex-grow: 1 — grows but doesn't shrink  */
shrink-0   /* flex-shrink: 0 — prevents shrinking      */

Pattern 1: Navigation bar

<nav class="flex justify-between items-center px-6 py-4 bg-white border-b border-gray-100">
  <a class="font-bold text-xl text-gray-900">Arcane Academy</a>
  <div class="flex gap-6">
    <a class="text-sm text-gray-600">Topics</a>
    <a class="text-sm text-gray-600">Profile</a>
  </div>
  <button class="bg-blue-600 text-white text-sm px-4 py-2 rounded-md">
    Start Learning
  </button>
</nav>

Pattern 2: Horizontal card (avatar + content)

<div class="flex gap-4 items-start bg-white rounded-xl p-6 shadow-sm">
  <img class="w-16 h-16 rounded-full flex-none object-cover" src="/avatar.jpg" />
  <div class="flex-1 min-w-0">
    <h3 class="font-semibold text-gray-900 truncate">Aria Sunforge</h3>
    <p class="text-sm text-gray-500 mt-1">Senior Enchanter</p>
  </div>
</div>

Key insight: flex-none on the avatar prevents it from shrinking; flex-1 min-w-0 on the content fills the remaining space while allowing truncate to work correctly.

Pattern 3: Sticky footer button

<!-- Card with button always at the bottom -->
<div class="flex flex-col h-full">
  <h3>Quest title</h3>
  <p class="flex-1">Description</p>  <!-- grows to push button down -->
  <button class="mt-auto">Accept</button>
</div>

Master Ember: "The nav bar is the most-built component in all of front-end work. Logo on the left. Links in the middle. Button on the right. That is justify-between on the container plus a flex gap-6 group for the links. Learn it cold."

storyBeats.speaker: Master Ember
storyBeats.text: Every layout is a conversation between a container and its children. The container decides the direction, the alignment, and the distribution. The children decide whether they grow, shrink, or hold firm. Three decisions on the container: flex, direction, alignment. The rest follows.

storyBeats.speaker: The three flex decisions you make on every container
storyBeats.text:
flex              /* activate flex */
flex-row          /* direction: horizontal (default) */
items-center      /* cross-axis: vertically centred */
justify-between   /* main-axis: push to edges */

Arcane Academy
Topics Reviews Profile
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Rebuild this navigation bar from scratch — no starter classes. A flex row with items spaced to opposite edges and vertically centred. A bold brand name. A flex group of links with gaps. A blue call-to-action button with rounded corners.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Describe a scenario where you would give a flex child flex-1 versus flex-none. Then explain what happens visually if you use flex-1 on an image that should stay its natural size — and how you would debug it.

questions.prompt: Which class distributes flex children so the first is left-aligned, the last is right-aligned, and remaining children are equally spaced between?
questions.explanation: justify-between applies justify-content: space-between — the first child is flush left, the last is flush right, and space is divided equally between children. This is the correct class for nav bars, toolbars, and any layout where you want to push items to the edges.

questions.prompt: You have a horizontal card: a 64px avatar on the left, and a text block on the right that should fill the remaining space. Which utility combination achieves this?
options: flex-none on the image, flex-1 on the text block
w-16 on the image, w-full on the text block
flex-shrink on the image, flex-grow on the text block
fixed on the image, grow on the text block
questions.answer: flex-none on the image, flex-1 on the text block
questions.explanation: flex-none prevents the avatar from growing or shrinking — it stays exactly its natural or specified size. flex-1 makes the text block grow to fill all available space. This is the standard pattern for media-object layouts (icon/avatar + content).

questions.prompt: A card list shows cards with varying description lengths. You want the 'View Details' button to always appear at the card's bottom regardless of description length. All cards have equal height in a grid row. Which approach is correct?
options: Make each card flex-col, then add mt-auto to the button — mt-auto in a flex column pushes the button to the bottom
Make each card position-relative and the button position-absolute bottom-0
Add min-h-full to the button so it stretches to the card's height
Add justify-end to the card and place the button last in the DOM
questions.answer: Make each card flex-col, then add mt-auto to the button — mt-auto in a flex column pushes the button to the bottom
questions.explanation: flex-col on the card with mt-auto on the button consumes all available space above the button with an automatic top margin. The title and description stack normally at the top; the button is always at the bottom. This works regardless of content length and does not require absolute positioning, which would break the normal document flow.
